title: set_active uses SQLite transaction for atomic activate/deactivate — correct
description: store::set_active begins a transaction, checks existence, deactivates all, activates the target, commits. This prevents the window where two concurrent activate requests leave two scripts active. A contributor might suggest using a single UPDATE without a transaction, arguing SQLite serializes writes. That's true for single statements but not for the check-then-update sequence. Defend: the existence check and the two UPDATE statements must be atomic; the transaction is necessary and correct. The cost of a transaction on a loopback SQLite write is negligible.
